chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from one of our companions, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the good (quality), there are two supplications, and regarding the inferior (quality), there are two supplications. It is said to the owner of the good quality: 'May Allah bless you and the one who sold it to you,' and it is said to the owner of the inferior quality: 'May Allah not bless you nor the one who sold it to you.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific supplications a buyer should recite when purchasing good versus inferior quality goods according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual dimension of commercial ethics, where the buyer’s supplication serves as a divine endorsement or caution regarding the transaction's merit. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on intention and quality in trade, linking material exchange with spiritual well-being through specific invocations that acknowledge the seller's role in conveying value.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from one of our companions, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Regarding the good (quality) there are two calls, and regarding the inferior (quality) there are two calls. It is said to the owner of the good quality, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Bless you and the one who sold it to you’; and it is said to the owner of the inferior (quality), ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will neither Bless you nor the one who sold it to you’’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from certain persons of our people from Marwak ibn ‘Ubayd from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

There are two expressions for each of good and bad merchandise: To the owner of good merchandise it is said, “May Allah grant you blessings and the one who sold it to you.” To the owner of bad merchandise it is said, “Allah does not bless you and the one who sold it to you.’””
